standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial abelian groups and associated chain complexes
standard_prerequisites.statement: The associated chain complex s(X) of a simplicial abelian group, its normalised complex N(X), and the definition of a quasi-isomorphism between them.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the setting and the acyclicity input (source lines 6055-6057, 6092-6095).

standard_prerequisites.name: Trivial Kan fibrations
standard_prerequisites.statement: The lifting property defining a trivial Kan fibration, expressed as the datum of the horn maps a and b (the author's definition-trivial-kan, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what the proof has to establish (source lines 6062-6073).

standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial groups are Kan complexes
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every simplicial group, in particular every simplicial abelian group, is a Kan complex (the author's lemma-simplicial-group-kan, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the horn filler x in degree n (source lines 6087-6088).

standard_prerequisites.name: The long exact sequence of homology
standard_prerequisites.statement: The long exact homology sequence of a short exact sequence of complexes (Homology, Lemma homology-lemma-long-exact-sequence-chain, declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: It shows that the kernel of f has vanishing homology, so that the reduction to Y = 0 stays a quasi-isomorphism (source lines 6080-6084).

core_obligations: Unwind the lifting problem: translate the solid diagram into the equations d_i x_j = d_{j-1} x_i and d_i y = f(x_i), and state the goal of producing x with d_i x = x_i and f(x) = y (source lines 6061-6073).

Reduce to a kernel: use termwise surjectivity to subtract a lift of y, so that one may assume y = 0 and f(x_i) = 0, i.e. replace X by the kernel of f; check with the long exact sequence that the kernel is still acyclic (source lines 6075-6084).
Fill the horn: use that a simplicial group is Kan to find x with the required faces and normalise the x_i to zero (source lines 6086-6091).

Use acyclicity: observe that the remaining x_n lies in the normalised complex and is a cycle, and that N(X) is quasi-isomorphic to s(X), so it is a boundary, which gives the required lift (source lines 6091-6099).

proof_roadmap.step: Translate the lifting problem into the simplex data and the goal.
Reduce to the kernel of f using termwise surjectivity and the long exact sequence.
Fill the horn by the Kan property and normalise the boundary data.
Conclude from the acyclicity of the normalised complex.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-qis-simplicial-abelian-groups at source lines 6053-6059: a termwise surjective homomorphism f : X to Y of simplicial abelian groups that induces a quasi-isomorphism on associated chain complexes is a trivial Kan fibration of simplicial sets. The proof at source lines 6061-6099 unwinds the lifting problem into the data x_0,...,x_n in degree n-1 and y in degree n, uses termwise surjectivity to subtract a lift of y and thereby reduce to the case where Y is zero and X is the kernel, invokes the long exact sequence to see that the kernel is acyclic, uses that X is a Kan complex to fill the horn, and finally reduces the remaining element to the normalised complex, where acyclicity makes it a boundary. It is short; the substance is the three reductions and the switch from s(X) to the normalised complex N(X).
